scoring_justification: The Purdy model is a deterministic calculation; the checker recomputes the reference ΔG_dis vs V_Mn curve from the agent’s CSV and compares using MAPE, qualifying as T1 recompute.

hidden_assets.purpose: Thermodynamic parameter ΔE=1.5 kJ/mol (half the chemical potential difference) used in the Purdy model
hidden_assets.source_provenance: Derived from Thermo-Calc calculation as referenced in the paper (not explicitly stated but used in the Purdy model). The reference solver uses this value to reproduce the dissipation curve shown in Figure 7a.
hidden_assets.generation_method: Obtained by running the paper’s reported Thermo-Calc step for the given steel composition at 640°C; the result 2ΔE = 3 kJ/mol (ΔE = 1.5 kJ/mol) is the standard value used in the hidden checker.
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: It is the actual value from the paper’s thermodynamic calculation, not an arbitrary number; it yields the dissipation curve consistent with the paper’s Figure 7a.

outputs.description: CSV containing the computed Gibbs free energy dissipation curve from the Purdy solute drag model. The hidden checker recomputes the same curve with exact parameters and compares using MAPE, with a threshold of 0.20; meeting or exceeding (MAPE ≤ 0.20) earns full credit.

steps.description: Score the agent’s Purdy model dissipation curve by recomputing the reference curve with the same model parameters and computing mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) over the log‑spaced V_Mn points, plus a shape check for peak location and monotonicity. Combined score: 80% MAPE, 20% shape. Full credit when MAPE ≤ 0.20 and shape valid.
